  "markdown_report": "The next experiment should establish reliable GRU context encoding before testing whether removing older history helps.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Matched prefix removal reduced training margins across all four categories. This challenges indiscriminate cropping but does not measure the effect of cropped training. (2) Padding discrepancies fell from roughly 1.6–2.0 to 0.0010–0.0023 in supplied results. Remaining discrepancies require numerical calibration before being classified as semantic errors. (3) Sampled pairwise separation is generally strong. It therefore provides limited evidence about competition near the benchmark’s top-10 boundary.

**Insights from related work.** (1) PyTorch documents recurrent terms and biases that remain active with zero inputs [1]. Padding must therefore be skipped explicitly, while ordinary floating-point variation requires separate controls [2]. (2) TimeSHAP studies attribution in recurrent sequences [3]. Paired deletions can expose model sensitivity without establishing users’ motives. (3) Krichene–Rendle distinguish sampled and full-catalog ranking metrics [4]. Supplementary catalog audits cannot replace the pinned selection metric.

The resulting directions are encoding correctness, controlled context intervention, and ranking-focused diagnosis:

| Layer | Existing evidence | Unresolved question | Proposed control |
|---|---|---|---|
| Encoding | Padding-dependent features | Recurrence, extraction, or numerical variation? | Unpadded reference and precision controls |
| Learning | Cropping loses matched margins | Harmful removal or useful regularization? | Matched-supervision training |
| Ranking | Positive sampled margins | Does top-10 membership improve? | Unchanged host HR@10 |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a positive and negative assessment.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Padding-calibrated matched cropping [1–3] | 4: interpretable combination; established components | 8: resolves a confound; gains uncertain | 5: fixed backbone; careful alignment |
| Full-context recency-weighted loss [3] | 3: atomic intervention; familiar weighting | 6: preserves history; may suppress useful targets | 2: simple weights; reduction needs care |
| Training-prefix top-10 boundary audit [4] | 3: targeted diagnosis; established ranks | 7: exposes weak competition; training optimism remains | 4: existing scorer; catalog cost |

**Selected idea: padding-calibrated matched cropping.** At 10% progress, prioritize a falsifiable experiment. First compare identical chronological histories against an unpadded reference, separating per-token recurrence, final readout, and candidate scores. Calibrate numerical error with repeated and batch-versus-singleton controls; investigate discrepancies in higher precision rather than relaxing tolerance retrospectively.

After encoding passes, compare unchanged training A, full-context matched suffix supervision B, and cropped-context identical supervision C. Freeze the existing half-history cropping policy, baseline objective, and full-context inference. C−B measures the training-context intervention; B−A measures supervision allocation. Neither contrast alone identifies stale interests.

Predeclare a common affordable schedule and select one complete condition by four-category macro validation HR@10. Deploy one checkpoint per category. Preserve seeds, routing, diagnosis interfaces, and predictor consistency; report incomplete comparisons if the shared budget prevents completion.

References: [1] [GRU](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html); [2] [numerical accuracy](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/notes/numerical_accuracy.md); [3] [TimeSHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00073); [4] [sampled metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).",
  "idea": {
    "description": "Test stochastic old-prefix removal only after calibrating GRU padding invariance. Compare unchanged training, full-context training with matched suffix supervision, and cropped-context training with the same suffix supervision as separate experimental conditions. Select one complete condition using four-category macro validation HR@10 and deploy exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category.",
    "motivation": "Supplied diagnostics show that removing old context lowers matched training margins, while residual padding discrepancies remain above the declared tolerance. These observations justify checking encoding and measurement semantics before interpreting context interventions. They neither establish that older history is harmful nor predict the effect of cropped training on validation HR@10. A small controlled experiment is appropriate at 10% research progress.",
    "implementation_notes": "Use the supplied corrected GRU4Rec rather than reconstructing its unavailable implementation. First diagnose existing padding behavior without changing it. Freeze one checkpoint, use evaluation mode and reset recurrent states for independent histories. Compare the same chronological real tokens under different left-padding lengths, batch companions, permutations and singleton evaluation. Compare valid-token outputs, final features and fixed-candidate scores separately. Measure absolute and relative discrepancies and ranking changes. Use repeated identical execution and batch-versus-singleton controls to characterize numerical variation. Investigate suspicious cases in FP32/FP64 with reduced-precision paths disabled where supported; do not retrospectively increase tolerance to force a pass. A failed tolerance alone does not identify the cause.

If a semantic recurrence defect is confirmed, fix it uniformly before all conditions. Compact nonpadding inputs chronologically into internally right-padded sequences, pack nonempty rows, run the original unidirectional GRU, unpack, and scatter valid outputs to their original B×L positions. Never pack left-padded tensors directly. Preserve the baseline's embeddings, dropout and recurrent layers. log2feats returns B×L×H. Read the greatest nonpadding index in the original layout, never count−1; handle empty rows explicitly. Update the embedded predictor writer and verify checkpoint-loaded predictor scores against training-model scores.

Predeclare A/B/C, common E≤200, 200 batches per epoch, final-epoch checkpoint selection, validation-query cap and charged time allocation within the remaining 43,200 GPU-second budget. Choose E using available charged timing evidence. If the complete comparison is unaffordable, report it as incomplete rather than presenting an unmatched contrast. Preserve the baseline optimizer, loss, dimensions and sampling semantics. For each row of n real inputs, retain all inputs unless a dedicated probability-0.5 branch draws K uniformly from ceil(n/2) through n inclusive; keep the final K real inputs. Empty rows have no loss and singleton rows remain unchanged. Actual removal probability is below 0.5.

A uses all baseline-valid supervised positions. B uses full input with supervision restricted to retained positions. C removes the prefix and uses exactly B's targets, negatives, position weights and reduction. Preserve target adjacency and all baseline negative-pool rules. Use separate crop randomness so it cannot alter initialization, batch sampling, negative sampling or dropout RNG consumption. Match crop plans and base samples across B/C; disclose any residual dropout differences rather than asserting identical stochastic trajectories. Log supervised-position counts and runtime because equal optimizer steps do not imply equal supervision or compute.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts and full permitted histories at inference. Select the complete condition with highest unchanged host macro validation HR@10; break exact ties A, then B, then C. Do not mix category winners, average checkpoints or combine scores. Each category loads exactly one independently trained model. No other-trial checkpoint reuse, hidden tests, extra data, pretrained weights or evaluator changes.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView interfaces. Use the actual trained view.model, restore its previous mode after probes, and accept (None, sequence, positive, negative) batches of B×L tensors. Return measured metrics and metric_definitions with counts and unavailable values. Context diagnostics are conditional training measurements, not validation HR@10. Use only histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; unavailable ratings, reviews, item categories, prices, stores, ownership and latent traits must not be inferred as observed. Preserve full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five per category. If host per-user validation hits are exposed, paired within-category bootstrap intervals may supplement aggregate contrasts; identify them as conditional on the fitted checkpoints and fixed candidates.",
    "pseudocode": "Predeclare A/B/C, p=0.5, minimum retained fraction=0.5,
common E<=200, 200 batches/epoch, final-checkpoint rule,
validation-query cap, and affordable charged budget.

Encoding gate:
  freeze a supplied GRU4Rec checkpoint; enter eval mode
  for fixed training histories:
    reference = evaluate chronological real inputs without padding
    compare equivalent padded and batched versions
    measure valid-state, final-feature and candidate-score errors separately
  calibrate against repeated-run and batch/singleton controls
  investigate discrepancies with precision controls
  if a semantic defect is confirmed:
    correct recurrence/readout uniformly in model and predictor writer
  if unresolved:
    report confounding; do not attribute effects to historical context

For condition in [A, B, C]:
  for category in required_four_categories:
    initialize the corrected baseline with seed 42
    reset dedicated base-sampling, negative-sampling and crop streams
    for epoch in range(E):
      for batch_index in range(200):
        _, x, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch(...)
        valid = baseline_valid_supervision_mask(x, positive, negative)
        keep = false_mask_like(x)
        for each nonempty row:
          positions = chronological_nonpadding_positions(x[row])
          n = len(positions)
          K = n
          if crop_rng.uniform() < 0.5:
            K = crop_rng.randint_inclusive(ceil(n/2), n)
          keep[row, positions[-K:]] = True
        context = x with positions outside keep zeroed if condition == C else x
        supervised = valid if condition == A else (valid & keep)
        features = padding_safe_GRU_log2feats(context)
        loss = baseline_objective(features, positive, negative,
                                  supervised, matched_B_C_reduction)
        update_one_model_using_baseline_schedule(loss)
    save final checkpoint and matching predictor artifacts
    run charged interface, padding and predictor-agreement checks
  obtain unchanged host four-category macro validation HR@10

Report C-B and B-A, category differences, supervision counts and charged time.
Choose one complete condition by macro HR@10; ties prefer A, then B, then C.
Deploy its one checkpoint per category, with full-context inference.
Never fuse condition scores or checkpoint parameters.",

      "positive": "Retains the GRU backbone and baseline objective, with input and supervision masks providing simple integration points.",
      "negative": "Numerical calibration, packed-output alignment, candidate matching, RNG separation and embedded predictor consistency require careful implementation."
    }
  },
